The question is not self-contained. In "Once they know it was Samson," the word "it" depends on the preceding story card for what Samson did; the question itself never mentions his burning the Philistines' crops.
"That place" has no antecedent within the question. Identifying the place where Samson fought requires earlier cards that are no longer on screen.

The question never identifies who "They" are. The preceding story card refers only to "the party" and "their hearts," so the question itself does not establish that the Philistines are bringing Samson out.
The question relies on "that spot," pointing back to the directions on story card 4, which is no longer on screen. Repeat the identifying context in the question so it stands on its own.

The question depends on "those men" without identifying them. Their identity appears only on the previous card, which the baker can no longer see; this question should identify them as the men who said Saul should not reign.

"If Saul hears that" points back to the Bethlehem excuse on the preceding story card. The question needs to summarize that excuse itself so it remains self-contained when the story card is no longer visible.

"That second day" relies on the preceding story card for its meaning. The question should identify the second day of the New Moon meal or month so the baker has the necessary context on the choice card itself.
The question begins, "By the time they've all gathered," but never identifies who "they" are. That antecedent is available only on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen.
The word "them" points back to David's father and mother on the previous card rather than identifying them within this question. The question should supply its own context.

The question does not stand on its own once the preceding story card disappears. "This stranger" does not identify Saul, and "his request" does not say that he asked the medium to consult a spirit and bring someone up.
The question depends on card 14 for essential context. "Those men" and "this" do not identify the men or their plan to withhold plunder from the two hundred who stayed behind.
"The woman" has no antecedent on the choice card. Without the previous story card, the question does not identify her as the woman David saw bathing from the palace roof.
"If the king asks all that" points back to Joab's expected questions on earlier cards instead of giving the necessary context on this card.
The phrase "on that rock" points back to the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to supply the rock and vigil context itself rather than relying on that reference.
The phrase "If Solomon walks that way" points back to earlier cards without explaining how Solomon is to walk. The question does not stand on its own.
The question never identifies Solomon or his sons as the ones who might turn away. It depends on the preceding story card to supply who is being warned.
The words "they" and "their" have no antecedent in the question. The baker must rely on earlier cards to know that Israel forsook the LORD and that the fathers were Israel's fathers.

Shown on its own, this question does not identify what the queen saw or what the report concerned. "She's seen it" and "the report" send the baker back to earlier cards for the basic context instead of naming Solomon and his wisdom and prosperity.
"This turn of events" points back to the preceding story card instead of identifying Rehoboam's refusal to listen to the people. The question does not supply its own context.
The question relies on earlier cards to identify "the warriors" as Rehoboam's forces and to explain what "this" refers to. Neither the who nor the what is established within the question itself.

The question is not self-contained: “that demand” points back to card 3, which is no longer visible, without restating that Ben-hadad has demanded Ahab's wealth and family. Put the demand in the question rather than referring back to the earlier card.
"That man" points back to the archer introduced only on card 9, so the question does not stand on its own when that story card is off screen.
"After that" points back to the feast and send-off on card 17 without identifying them in the question. The question should name the event it refers to so it stands alone.
The question depends on 'that story,' pointing back to card 11 instead of identifying Gehazi's account of Elisha bringing the dead back to life. The earlier card is no longer on screen.

The phrases 'about it' and 'the story' never identify what the king asks the woman to confirm. The question needs to supply the context that Gehazi has identified her and the son Elisha restored to life.

The question depends on "Hazael hears this" and "such a monstrous thing," but it never says what Elisha has just told him. These phrases point back to card 12, so the question does not supply its own context once that story card is off screen.
The phrase "that plot of ground" has no antecedent within the question and depends on the preceding cards, which are no longer on screen. The question needs to identify Naboth's plot itself.

The question begins with “They” without identifying the people of the land. The pronoun's antecedent is only on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen, so the question does not supply its own context.
The question is not self-contained. "Them" refers to the people around the king, who are identified only on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen.
The question's "they" has no antecedent within the question. Identifying who acts depends on earlier cards that are no longer visible.
"After that" points back to the preceding story card about Zedekiah's eyes being put out, so the question does not supply that context itself.
"Them all" has no antecedent in the question. The baker must rely on the preceding story card to know that Nebuzaradan is bringing the priests and other officials.

Several questions do not carry their own context. Card 12 relies on "the three tribes," card 14 on "that battle," card 18 on "these families," and card 20 on "these tribes," rather than identifying the people or event within the question.
The question does not identify who "them" refers to. Its antecedent is on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible, so the question lacks the context needed to stand on its own.
The question depends on the preceding story card to identify "The crown." Once that card is gone, the question does not say that this is the crown David took from the Ammonite king.
The question does not identify David or Solomon. "This son" depends on earlier cards that are no longer visible, so the question does not supply its own context.
The wording "While they praise the LORD" leaves "they" without an antecedent within the choice card. It points back to the trumpeters and singers on earlier cards that the baker can no longer see.

The question leaves "them" unidentified and omits the shut skies and lack of rain. Without the previous story card on screen, the question does not establish who Solomon is asking God to forgive or the drought context that makes "rain" a reasoned answer.

"That enemy land" and "they" point back to the previous story card. The question never identifies the captive Israelites who have come to their senses and returned to God, so it is not self-contained.

Several questions rely on antecedents from cards that are no longer visible. Card 5 says "hard days like that," card 7 says "do all that," card 16 says "If it comes to that," and card 17 says "did this" without identifying the disaster in the question.

The question begins with "They," but never identifies who they are. With the preceding story card no longer on screen, the baker cannot tell from the question whether this means the priests and Levites, the people from every tribe, or all the newcomers together.
The question uses "they" without identifying who returns to Jerusalem, so it depends on the previous story card for its subject. It should name Jehoshaphat and the men of Judah and Jerusalem.
The phrase "Along with that help" points back to the preceding card instead of making the question self-contained. The question should restate the assistance Cyrus has just described.
"They" has no antecedent within the question. The question relies on card 1 to identify the returning exiles instead of supplying that context itself.
"When they arrive" has no antecedent within the question. It should identify the returned exiles rather than depending on earlier cards to establish who "they" are.

"That crowd" points back to earlier cards without identifying the crowd gathered at the temple foundation. The question does not supply its own who-and-what context, especially if it returns by itself during mistake correction.
The question never identifies who 'they' are. 'Their offer' and 'they say' rely on the preceding card instead of naming the enemies of Judah and Benjamin so the question can stand alone.
'Their big finish' has no antecedent within the question. The baker must rely on the preceding card to know that this means Rehum and Shimshai's letter to Artaxerxes.
"All these supplies" points back to the list on the preceding card rather than giving the needed context within this question. The question should identify the supplies or otherwise stand on its own.

"For the dedication they offer" relies on the preceding story card to explain both who "they" are and what is being dedicated. The question does not independently identify the people of Israel or the dedication of the house of God.
'Dressed like that' depends on card 12's description of Mordecai's royal garments and crown, which is no longer on screen. The question is not self-contained.
The question depends on "that day" without identifying the thirteenth of Adar. Its immediate story card does not supply the date either, so a baker seeing only the question lacks the full context.

The question refers to Job's "own question" without restating that he wondered whether God would contend with him in His great power. It therefore relies on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible, for essential context.
The phrase "this decree" has no antecedent within the question. The question needs to identify it as God's decree against Job rather than relying on the preceding story card.

The phrase "all this" points back to earlier cards without giving the baker the context needed to reason out Job's response. The question should briefly identify what Job is considering, such as God's unchangeability and His decree against Job.
The phrase "these people" relies on earlier cards for its referent. The question should identify them as the people who rebel against the light so that it stands on its own.
The phrase "these sinners" depends on the preceding card to identify the group. The question should briefly supply that context, such as the sinners whom Sheol steals away.
"Nobody alive has it" does not identify what "it" is. The question relies on earlier cards rather than naming wisdom in its own context.

The question relies on "these people" from earlier cards without identifying them. Standing alone, it should identify them as the people crying out under oppression so the baker has the necessary context.
The question relies on the previous story card to identify "that corrupt crowd." Once that story card is off screen, the question does not identify whose crowd David is describing.

"In that last verse" points back to the setup on card 14. The question should stand on its own by identifying the psalm's final verse directly rather than relying on a story card the baker can no longer see.
"People like that" has no antecedent within the question. Once the earlier cards are off screen, the question does not identify which people David calls a generation.

The question relies on "that man's" to point back to the preceding cards instead of identifying the man itself. It should identify him as the man who fears the LORD so the question remains self-contained.
"Right after that promise" points back to story card 6, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to supply the promise's context itself rather than referring to it as "that promise."

The phrase "a moment like that" points back to card 1 without supplying its context. Standing alone, the question does not say that David had pretended to be insane before Abimelech and been driven away.

The phrase "all that shaking" points back to earlier cards without identifying what the shaking is. The question needs its own context, such as the transformed earth, toppled mountains and roaring waters, because those earlier cards are no longer on screen.

"Right after that" points back to the previous card without saying what happened. The question should supply the context of the nations raging, kingdoms crumbling and the earth melting when God lifts His voice.
The question begins with 'Their' without saying whose lands and homes these are. The antecedent depends on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen.
The phrase 'this fate' does not explain what fate is being discussed. Without the preceding story card, the question lacks the context needed to stand on its own.
The question depends on "they" and "that man" from the preceding story card. On its own, it does not identify the people who are threatening the man, so it lacks the required context.
"These people" points back to people identified on an earlier card. The question should identify them itself as the people intending to cast the man down.

'Right after that' points back to card 6 without giving its context. The question does not independently restore the moment about the one God chooses and brings near, so it does not stand on its own once the earlier card is gone.
The question is not self-contained: “praying this way” points back to the table-snare and wrath requests on story card 5 without telling the baker what manner of prayer it means.
“Those cities” points back to the preceding choice card instead of identifying the cities of Judah in the question, so the question does not supply its own context.
"After an offer like that" points back to the preceding cards without saying what the offer was, so the question does not supply its own context.

"Right after those names" points back to the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen. The question should supply its own context by naming Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna or otherwise identifying the people meant.

"After the fire picture" relies on the preceding story card without restating what that picture was. The question should briefly supply the image of fire consuming a forest and setting the mountains ablaze so it is self-contained.
The question begins with 'Then he' without identifying the singer. Its antecedent depends on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen.
Cards 16, 17 and 19 refer only to "that generation" without identifying which generation within the question. Each question therefore depends on context from cards that are no longer on screen.
The question uses "them" and "they" without identifying Moses, Aaron and Samuel, so it depends on earlier cards that are no longer visible.
"These same men" has no antecedent within the question. The question needs to identify Moses, Aaron and Samuel rather than rely on earlier cards.
The question does not identify who "them" and "their" refer to, leaving its context dependent on the preceding choice card.
The question never identifies the LORD as the one meant by "His," so its wording still points back to the preceding story card for context.

The question's all this does not identify which actions it means and therefore depends on earlier cards that are no longer visible. It should specify the relevant events, such as God bringing Israel out of Egypt and providing for His people in the desert.
The standalone question does not identify who "they" are. It should name God's people or the captives rather than relying on context from an earlier card.
The question says "her door" without identifying the forbidden woman. Since the earlier cards are no longer on screen, the pronoun leaves the question without the required context.

The question's "her house" relies on the preceding story card to identify the woman. Because that card is no longer visible, the question should identify her itself, such as by saying "the woman's house."
The question's "her house" points back to the preceding story card and does not identify whose house it is. The question should supply that context itself, such as by saying "the woman's house."
"That bear" points back to the bear introduced on story card 4, which is no longer on screen. The question should stand alone, for example by saying "a bear robbed of her cubs."
"Right before that" points back to the previous story card's keep/discard line, which is no longer on screen. The question should provide that context itself rather than rely on an unseen antecedent.
The question begins "Say that man..." without identifying the man within the question. "That man" points back to earlier cards that are no longer on screen.
"That man" has no antecedent within the question. The question relies on earlier cards to identify the man being compared with the stillborn child instead of supplying that context itself.

The question points back to the preceding story card with "In that same line" instead of restating the Teacher's saying about endings and beginnings. It should supply that context itself so it stands alone when the story card is no longer visible.
The question's 'this' points back to the previous story card's list of outcomes. Without that card on screen, the question does not say what time and chance are explaining.

"In that day" depends on an earlier card for its antecedent. The question should identify the Day of the LORD itself so that its context remains clear when the preceding story card is no longer on screen.
"He" and "his kingdom" depend on the child mentioned on card 14, but that story card is no longer visible. The question needs to identify the child itself.
"All of this" points back to the kingdom description on card 16, which is no longer visible. The question never says what the people's own strength is supposedly accomplishing.
The question depends on "those cities," but the list appears on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible. It should restate the relevant comparison instead of pointing back to that card.
"That picture of the axe" points back to card 7, which is not on screen when the baker answers. The question should include the picture of the axe and the one swinging it so that it stands alone.
The word 'there' leaves the location unstated and relies on an earlier card to supply 'God's holy mountain.' The question should include that context itself.

The phrase 'these terrified people' has no antecedent within the question and points back to the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to establish the moment itself, such as the terror and anguish accompanying the Day of the LORD.
“That throne” has no antecedent within the question and points back to card 5. The question should identify the throne in its own context rather than relying on a card the baker can no longer see.

The question refers to "all this" without identifying the desolation of the strong cities. That needed context is available only on the preceding story card, so the question does not stand on its own.

The phrase "this sudden end" points back to the preceding card rather than giving the context within the question. It should identify the raging nations' sudden terror in the evening and their being no more before morning.

The people in distress are referred to only as "their," "them" and "they." The question never identifies them as the singers or God's people, so it depends on an earlier card to establish who is being discussed.

The question is not self-contained. “Him” is meant to refer to the Rabshakeh, but he is never mentioned in the question, so the pronoun depends on an earlier card; the only person named in this question is Hezekiah.
"This one" has no antecedent within the question. The baker must remember card 13 to know that it means the Servant, so the question does not supply its own context.
The question begins "He burns" without identifying the woodworker. Once the preceding story card is off screen, the pronoun has no self-contained context.
The question relies on "He" and "that wood" instead of identifying the woodworker and the wood he used. It depends on earlier cards that are no longer visible rather than supplying its own context.
The question depends on "that wild donkey" in the preceding story card and does not identify the donkey as a picture of Israel. It does not supply enough context on its own.
The question never identifies who "them" and "they" refer to. Without the preceding story card, it does not make clear that the LORD is judging Israel.
The question begins "That silver and gold," using "that" to point back to the previous story card instead of restating the context, such as the silver from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz.
The question uses "that wound" and "it" to point back to the preceding story card instead of supplying the wound's context within the question itself.

Cards 4, 10 and 11 use "their" or "them" without identifying the people, and card 6 begins with "that oath" even though its antecedent was on the preceding story card. These questions rely on cards that are no longer visible instead of supplying their own context.

Card 8 does not identify who "these people" are, card 12 refers back to "that beautiful olive tree" without establishing the picture in the question, and card 13 does not identify who "the people" are. These questions are not self-contained once the preceding story cards disappear.
"That nation" points back to the preceding story card. Without that card, the question does not retell the setup that the LORD had announced He would build up and establish the nation.

The question asks why the LORD says "this" without restating the wormwood and poisoned-water judgment. It relies on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible, instead of giving the needed context in the question.

The question is not self-contained: "all this" points back to the judgments described on earlier cards without identifying them. When those cards are no longer visible, the question does not adequately say what the LORD will do.
The question refers to "the city" without identifying it as Jerusalem. Understanding which city was breached depends on earlier cards that are no longer on screen.
"They" has no antecedent within the question. Knowing that it means Nebuzaradan and the Babylonian officials depends on story card 10, which is no longer on screen.

The question depends on card 3, which is no longer visible. "That message," "the men" and "it" do not identify the warning about going to Egypt or the leaders making the accusation, so the question is not self-contained.

The question begins, "Once the LORD saves them," but the antecedent of "them" is found only on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen. The question should identify Jacob and his descendants itself.
"In that hard line" and "who else" depend on story card 15, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to restate the first curse so that it stands on its own.

"In that day" points back to card 8 for the capture of Kirioth and the seizure of the strongholds, but that story card is no longer on screen. The question needs to carry those events itself so the baker has the context for the warriors' reaction.

The question asks about "the calamity on this nation" without identifying the nation. Its subject depends on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen, so the question does not supply its own context.

The question never identifies who “them” and “they” are. Their antecedent appears only on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible, so the question does not independently establish that it is about Babylon's people.
The question never names Jerusalem or otherwise identifies the city. Its opening "She" depends on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible.

The question refers only to "Him," relying on the preceding story card to identify the figure on the throne in Ezekiel's vision. Once that story card is off screen, the question does not supply the required context.

"Inside that hidden room" and "all those engravings" point back to cards 11-12, which are no longer on screen. The question also never names Ezekiel or freshly establishes the scene, so it is not self-contained.
The question does not identify who "they" are; that depends on remembering the preceding story card. Name the city or its people in the question itself.
"They" and "them" rely on earlier cards to identify the house of Israel. The question needs to name the house of Israel itself.
"Them" has no antecedent within the question, so the question does not identify whom God says He will gather. Name the house of Israel.
Both uses of "they" depend on earlier cards to identify who will be melted within the city. The question should name the house of Israel.
The question never identifies who "them" refers to. It depends on the earlier story card about the men portrayed on the wall, so it is not self-contained when that card is no longer visible.

"Through all of this" does not identify the judgment, and "Her" in the answers has no named antecedent in the question. The question needs to name Oholibah and give the judgment context rather than point back to earlier cards.

"God gives the reason" and "all of this" leave the events being explained unidentified without the preceding cards. The question should establish that God is explaining the judgment coming on Oholibah.

The question never identifies whose stronghold, pride and joy, and sons and daughters are meant by 'their.' The antecedent appears only on earlier cards, so the question should name Israel or the house of Israel and stand on its own.
"After that list" points back to story card 8, which is no longer on screen, without giving the baker enough context to know what list the question means.
"When it all comes to pass" depends on story card 9 for the meaning of "it all." The question does not supply that context itself, and the previous story card is no longer visible.

The question refers to "what people said" and "the land" without giving the people's accusation or identifying the land as Israel's. It relies on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen, for that context.

The question uses "all this" to point back to the tendons, flesh, skin and breath described on story card 9. Since that card is no longer on screen, the question does not provide the needed context itself.

The question begins 'In that square inner court', using 'that' to point back to the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen. The question should supply its own context without that backward reference.

The question begins with "That gate" but never identifies the gate within the question. Its antecedent is on an earlier card, so the question does not stand on its own; it should name the inner court's east gate.
"These offerings" and "this place" have no antecedents within the question. The baker must look back to earlier cards to know which offerings and which place the statement means.
"These" has no antecedent within the question. The question should identify the four corner courts, or the courts containing the ovens, rather than relying on the preceding card.

The question relies on the previous card for its essential context: “live this way” does not explain that Nebuchadnezzar will be driven away from mankind and feed on grass like an ox. Seen on its own, the question does not say what condition Daniel is describing.

The question relies on “this” to supply the accusation from the preceding story card. By itself, it never says what Darius hears about Daniel, so the choice lacks the context needed to understand the moment.
"That king" points back to the preceding choice card for its identity. The question needs to identify him within itself, for example as the king who spoke against the Most High.
"His" and "Him" have no antecedent within the question. The question should name whose kingdom is everlasting and whom the rulers will serve and obey.

The question begins with the unidentified pronoun "He." The person taking the captives is identified only on the preceding choice card, so the question does not supply its own context when that card is no longer visible.

"Hosea asks this of his wife" does not explain what "this" means. The requirement being discussed appears only on card 9, so this question relies on a card the baker can no longer see instead of supplying its own context.

Several choice cards do not identify their subject independently. Cards 12, 15 and 17 use them or they without an antecedent; cards 13 and 14 say only the people; and card 19 depends on the phrase These are the same people. Without the earlier cards on screen, these questions do not clearly identify Ephraim or Israel.

The question relies on the previous story card for its context: “that heifer” does not identify Ephraim or explain the picture within the question itself. Make the question self-contained so it does not point back to a card the baker can no longer see.

The question begins, "Micah keeps that rough picture going," using "that" to refer back to the violent picture on story card 4, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to supply that context itself or omit the backward reference.

"Those peoples" has no antecedent within the question and points back to story card 10, which is no longer on screen. The question should identify them as the peoples Zion breaks to pieces or the nations gathered against her.
The question never identifies whose possessions are being removed. The pronouns "their" and "them" depend on "His people" in the preceding story card, which is no longer visible.

The question does not identify whose cities and strongholds these are. "Their" has no clear antecedent within the question itself and relies on context from earlier cards that the baker can no longer see.

"In this picture" depends on the preceding story card and does not identify the picture as Habakkuk's description of God measuring the earth and startling the nations. The question does not supply enough context on its own.
"All that marching" points back to the preceding story card. Standing alone, the question does not explain that the LORD marched across the earth with fury and threshed the nations in wrath.
"Those warriors" has no antecedent within the question. The card needs to identify them as the wicked one's warriors who stormed out to scatter Habakkuk's people.
"It all" leaves what Habakkuk heard undefined without the preceding story card. The question should identify the report and picture of the LORD's coming that Habakkuk has heard.
The question does not explain what event 'When this happens' refers to, and 'the one who is speaking' does not adequately identify the speaker. Both depend on cards that are no longer on screen.
The question relies on "that third" pointing back to earlier cards. Standing alone, it does not identify the group as the third left in the land.

"In that secret meeting" points back to the setup on card 13, which is no longer on screen. The question should supply the context itself, such as by saying that Herod is meeting secretly with the Magi.
"That report" points back to card 16 without explaining the report in this question. The question should say that Herod wants the Magi to report to him after they find the Child.
The question is not self-contained. "This fulfilled" points back to the preceding story card for its antecedent; the question itself never identifies what Matthew says was fulfilled.
The question depends on card 15 to explain what “it” is. Without that card on screen, the question does not identify the dispute with the adversary or the trip to court.

"Those people" has no antecedent within the question. The question needs to identify the people who will tell Jesus on that day about the works they did in His name, rather than relying on the preceding story card.
"Them" has no antecedent within the question. The people Jesus is addressing need to be identified in the question itself.

The question relies on the unidentified 'they' for who asks Jesus. The preceding story cards do not identify that group either, and they are no longer visible when the baker answers, so the question does not supply its own context.
The question ends with “upon them,” but never identifies who “them” is. The baker must rely on earlier cards to know that Jesus is addressing the Pharisees; name that audience in the question itself.
The question refers only to "they" without identifying the Pharisees and scribes, so the baker must rely on an earlier card to know whom Jesus is addressing.

The question's "this" points back to Peter's confession on the previous story card, but the question never identifies what was revealed. Since that story card is no longer on screen, the question should supply the content itself: Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God.

The phrase "in the same way" depends on the preceding story card's account of people doing whatever they wished to Elijah. The question itself never supplies that comparison, so it should restate enough of card 6 to stand on its own.

The question relies on the preceding story card: “that cup and dish” points back to context the baker can no longer see. It should itself explain that Jesus is addressing the scribes and Pharisees, who clean the outside of the cup and dish.

“That line of righteous blood” depends entirely on the preceding story card. The question should supply the needed context itself: Jesus is speaking about all the righteous blood shed on earth, extending to Zechariah.

The opening 'that servant' depends on the preceding story card to identify the faithful and wise servant. Since that card is no longer visible, the question needs to identify the servant and his assignment within its own wording.

"If the servant knew all that" relies on the preceding story card to identify which servant is meant and what "all that" refers to. The question is not self-contained once that story card is off screen.
"When he hears this" depends on Jesus' statement on the preceding story card without identifying what that statement was. The choice does not provide its own context for the high priest's reaction.

The question is not self-contained. "The man like that" depends on the previous card's description of the man as sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; on its own, the question does not identify which man or explain what "like that" means.
"Jesus takes it even further" uses "it" to point back to the preceding card's teaching rather than giving that context within the question.

The question is not self-contained. In "Once the centurion confirms it," the antecedent of "it" is that Jesus is already dead, but that appears only on earlier cards. The question should state what the centurion confirms.
The question does not identify who "the two" are or what they report with "it." Both depend on earlier cards that the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

examples: Genesis 24:67 says that Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent, but the walkthrough never supplies that fact. Card 19 only rules out Abraham's tent, and this card moves straight to the marriage, love and comfort, leaving an important detail of the verse untaught.

The walkthrough never tells Onan's actual action in verse 9: whenever he slept with Tamar, he spilled his seed on the ground. Cards 8-10 give only his knowledge and the result that no offspring was produced, then refer to "what Onan did" without explaining the deed. This omits a central detail and leaves verse 10 less clear.

Joseph's actual reaction in Genesis 50:17, weeping when the message arrives, is never told. Marking anger as false only says what he did not do and leaves an important detail of the reconciliation uncovered.
